facts.text: Pahoa boasts the highest concentration of century‑old buildings in all of Hawaii, giving the town a uniquely historic feel.
Before the 1955 blaze, a sugar cane and tofu factory dominated Pahoa’s economy, shaping the town’s early industrial character.
A wood‑fired furnace at the tofu factory ignited a fire in 1955 that nearly destroyed Pahoa, but a local’s water truck saved the town.
Volcanic soils beneath Pahoa were laid down by Kīlauea eruptions within the last 125 to 500 years, shaping the fertile landscape.
During the 2014 Kīlauea eruption, lava reached Pahoa’s recycling facility before stopping short of Route 130, sparing the town’s main road.
The Pahoa Library, part of the Hawaii State Public Library System, provides residents with access to books, computers, and community programs.
